name: Eshcol
overview: Eshcol was a male Amorite known as 'the Amorite,' indicating his tribal affiliation. He is briefly mentioned in Genesis 14:13, with no additional personal notes provided. His identity is primarily established by his connection to the Amorite people.
namesAndTitles: The name Eshcol means 'cluster of grapes,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name. This meaning is noted in Genesis 14:13 and does not appear to be a name given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eshcol as having brothers named Mamre and Aner, both inferred from the same passage in Genesis 14:13. He is also identified as a descendant of Amor and is noted to be an ally of Abram, highlighting important familial and covenantal connections.
scriptureSignificance: Eshcol's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his role as an Amorite ally of Abram during a time of conflict. His association with Abram underscores the alliances formed between Abram and local tribal leaders. Though briefly mentioned, Eshcol's presence contributes to the broader understanding of tribal relations and support networks in Abram's story.
